Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 3.4125989 (a root of x³ − 15x² + 75x − 121) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.25036321π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 0.12054152 (a root of x³ − 24/13x² + 11/13x − 1/13) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.88892298π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g2 − 4| + |tr[g2, g1·g2] − 2| ≈ 0.75 < 1. ⟨g2, g1·g2⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g2, g1·g2] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1·g2⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).
